data.name: Amethyst
data.gender_notes: Amethyst is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word amethystos, meaning 'not intoxicated'. In ancient Greece, amethyst was believed to protect against drunkenness and intoxication. This name is also associated with the spiritual qualities of wisdom, clarity, and peace. The name Amethyst carries the meaning “Purple gemstone” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Amethyst usually hope their child will grow to embody purple gemstone and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of spiritual clarity and wisdom.
data.etymology: Amethyst belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Purple gemstone.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Amethyst total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_hebrew.name: אמטיסט
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם אמטיסט אינו מופיע ישירות בתנ"ך העברי. עם זאת, הוא קשור למונח היווני 'אמטיסטוס' (αμέθυστος), שפירושו 'לא שיכור'. מקורו של השם קשור למסורת היוונית לפיה האבן אמטיסט נוצרה כדי למנוע שכרות.

in_greek.name: Αμέθυστος
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Αμέθυστος προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη 'αμέθυστος', που σημαίνει 'ακράτητος' ή 'μη μεθυσμένος'. Στην ελληνική παράδοση, ο αμέθυστος ήταν μια πέτρα που πιστευόταν ότι προστατεύει από τη μέθη. Ο όρος συνδέεται με την ιστορία της εκκλησίας και την παράδοση των αγίων ονομάτων.
